### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. giant axonal neuropathy 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.399)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8951664)

**Proposed mechanism:** CCDC22 (HGNC:25940) —DISRUPTS→ Ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000422); DCAF8 (HGNC:28663) —DISRUPTS→ Ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000422); Ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000422) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000422) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0002670); Ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000422) —LEADS_TO→ Peripheral neuropathy (HP:0003688); Ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000422) —LEADS_TO→ Global developmental delay (HP:0001263). Loss-of-function mutations in CCDC22 (Ritscher-Schinzel syndrome 2) and DCAF8 (giant axonal neuropathy 2) both converge on disrupting the ubiquitin-proteasome system, leading to a shared downstream phenotype of intellectual disability, skeletal abnormalities, peripheral neuropathy, and global developmental delay.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in CCDC22 and DCAF8 that result in gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects, or a complete lack of overlap in the downstream consequences of disrupting the ubiquitin-proteasome system for both genes. _(variant: Analysis of gnomAD data revealing common variants in CCDC22 or DCAF8 associated with loss-of-function phenotypes that are not present in the general population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CCDC22 and DCAF8 in the ubiquitin-proteasome system could reveal common therapeutic targets for neurodevelopmental and neurological disorders associated with protein degradation pathway dysfunction. Modulating the ubiquitin-proteasome system could offer a unified therapeutic strategy.
